records.new_description: 2020 July 20: Brunei's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a Statement on the South China Sea reaffirming its 'two-step approach', that 'specific issues should be addressed bilaterally by the countries directly concerned through peaceful dialogue and consultations' and that 'such negotiations on the South China Sea should be resolved in accordance with the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)', calling for restraint and an early Code of Conduct (mfa.gov.bn, Press Room 841; VietnamNet/VNA, 22 July 2020), a week after the US position of 13 July 2020. The first stand-alone MFA press release on the South China Sea in the ministry's record (2005 on); the 2016 response to the arbitral award was a deputy minister's interview. It asserts no Bruneian right or zone and names no state.

records.new_description: 2003 March: after Malaysia had licensed deepwater Blocks L and M to Murphy Oil in January 2003 over the same acreage as Brunei's Blocks J and K (awarded in February 2002 after the 2001 licensing round), Brunei signed the Block J production-sharing agreement with Total, BHP Billiton and Amerada Hess on 10 March 2003 (Total press release of that date, SEC Form 6-K; BHP Billiton Form 20-F 2005) and sent a patrol craft to drive Murphy's drilling ship out of the disputed area; the next month Malaysian gunboats blocked a Total vessel, and both sides halted work pending talks that began with the Sultan and Mahathir in May (Straits Times/FEER, 3 July 2003; AFP via Malaysiakini, 14 July 2003; Energy Intelligence, 9 June 2003; Al Jazeera/Reuters, 22 August 2003). The first known Bruneian naval enforcement against a rival's licensee, and licensing pressed in the face of a rival licence: coercive (physical interference), a new method. The Block K contract with the Shell-led group followed later in 2003.
records.edit_summary: In March 2003, after Malaysia had licensed Blocks L and M over the same acreage in January, Brunei signed the production-sharing agreement for deepwater Block J with a Total-led consortium (10 March) and sent a patrol craft to drive a Murphy Oil drilling ship from the disputed area; Block K went to a Shell-led consortium later in 2003.
